tasks.design: Configure native source/version links and construction-plan fields in {PROJECT}, {DOCS} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. The specialist retains planning and coordination, captures actual agreements, checks the final plan and separately saves and distributes it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Planning can repeat source navigation and stable plan references.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked sources and plan fields can reduce navigation and duplicate identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Safe staging and operational coordination depend on actual airfield constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognises operational conflicts that a plan field cannot resolve.
tasks.altitude: Less plan administration; airfield construction judgement stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native project/document links and plan fields can support construction coordination; they do not authorise airfield work or determine safe staging.

assumptions: Actual engineering/operations owners supply versioned drawings, scope and restrictions; specialist checks relevance in s1. Actual field assessments, staging choices and stakeholder agreements remain in s2/s3.
S4 reduces stable identifiers and repeated source references only; actual agreement capture and full final check stay within retained 10.4 hours. Missing actual restrictions remain manual.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native fields first; existing automatic references earn zero saving. Save and send each retain one percent using existing final check.

Distribution covers coordinated planning within actual authority; work permission, airfield closure and construction release are separate exact-final-plan decisions by actual authorised owners, with no avoided labour claimed. Only actual plan revisions/distributions are counted.
unknowns: Which plan navigation and repeated fields remain manual?
research_questions: Can native fields reduce administration after complete operational review?

tasks.design: Configure native flight/stand/service views in {OPS_SYSTEM} using actual current source records. The specialist verifies freshness, retains all active monitoring and operational assessment, and captures/checks any actual required monitoring entry before committing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Monitoring context may require repeated navigation through operational status screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native joined status views can reduce navigation when source identities and timestamps match.
tasks.still_hard: Safe monitoring needs actual observation and interpretation of changing conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognises that a displayed service state does not match the actual airfield.
tasks.altitude: Less status navigation; active monitoring stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native operational status views can consolidate existing flight/stand/service records; they do not establish actual completion or replace airfield monitoring.

assumptions: Actual flight/service owners supply flight identity, stand, event/service status, observation time and source freshness. Specialist checks them in s1; absent/stale feeds fall back to actual communication and observation, with no assumed integration saving.

Only repeated screen navigation loses time. Continuous attention, actual observation, source ambiguity and intervention decisions remain fully retained. No surveillance interpretation or automated clearance is assumed.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native views first; existing consolidated access earns zero saving. S3/s4 represent only an actual required log; if none exists omit and reweight, without inventing administration.

Actual alerts, instructions or clearances each need a separate exact-content decision/send step if included in another duty; no avoided send time is claimed. Log commit retains one percent and uses existing final check.
unknowns: Are actual service statuses reliably timestamped?
research_questions: Can native views reduce navigation without reducing monitoring attention?

incremental.description: Maintain actual operational view mappings and freshness checks.

tasks.design: Configure native current-procedure and resource links in {LMS} and {DOCS}. The specialist checks objectives, retains explanation, demonstration, practice and assessment, then captures actual training results and separately commits the checked record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training preparation may repeat navigation to current procedures and resources.
tasks.enabler_now: Native procedure/resource links can shorten actual preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Operational competence requires observed practice and feedback.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer notices unsafe understanding despite a plausible verbal answer.
tasks.altitude: Less preparation navigation; training and competence judgement stay human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native learning/document links can support current-procedure preparation; they do not establish staff competence.

assumptions: Actual procedure owners supply current versions and existing training resources; specialist checks relevance/objectives in s1. No free lesson design, observation capture or assessment is assumed.
All delivery, supervised practice, evaluation and actual record capture remain retained. Preparation is counted once per actual prepared/revised session rather than per participant or conversation.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native links first; existing linked access earns zero saving. Actual training record only; if none required omit and reweight. Commit retains one percent and uses existing final check; no automatic certification or separate release is assumed.
research_questions: Can native resources reduce navigation while preserving actual staff practice?

tasks.design: Configure native contact/responsibility links in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}. Retain actual agency coordination and agreement capture, then separately commit any actual support record and send any actual required written request after final checking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency coordination can repeat contact and responsibility navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native current-contact and support-context links can shorten preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Actual agency commitments and operational conflicts require direct coordination.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist negotiates feasible support and recognises unresolved operational dependencies.
tasks.altitude: Less agency lookup; coordination stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native contact/responsibility links can support agency preparation; they do not establish an agency commitment or airfield authority.

assumptions: Actual agency/airfield owners supply current contacts, responsibilities and requirements; specialist checks them in s1. Actual support discussion and capture remain in s2/s3, with no inferred agreement or completed support.
Only lookup navigation loses time. Existing current directory access earns zero saving. Native links first; no automated operational instruction is proposed.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Record and written request branches apply only when actually required; oral-only coordination removes them and reweights actual work rather than inventing administration.

Commit/send each retain one percent and consume the existing final check after content exists. Actual authority/recipient restrictions are checked before send. Shared construction coordination under 10614 is counted once.
research_questions: Can native current links reduce preparation without reducing agency coordination?
